business_model.basis: stated in the 20-F Item 4 business overview
business_model.claim: The company owns and operates crude oil tankers, Suezmax and VLCC, and sells seaborne crude oil transportation. It describes its Eco fleet as fuel-efficient and fitted with scrubbers.
quotes: We are an international owner and operator of a modern, fuel-efficient Eco fleet of 16 tanker vessels, comprising eight modern Suezmax tankers and eight modern VLCC tankers, focusing on the transportation of crude oil.

business_model.claim: Revenue comes from time charters and voyage charters. Under a voyage (spot) charter the customer pays a transportation charge for a specific cargo and the company pays the voyage expenses. Under a time charter the vessel is leased for a set period and the charterer bears voyage expenses.
quotes: Revenues include revenues from time charters and voyage charters.
Voyage charters or spot voyages are charters under which the customer pays a transportation charge for the movement of a specific cargo between two or more specified ports.

business_model.basis: stated in Item 4 (employment column of the fleet table and the February charter); the spot-dominated reading is inferred from that column
business_model.claim: Almost all vessels in the fleet table are employed on spot or short-term business. Only one vessel is shown on a 12-month term, and a one-year time charter for it was announced with a global commodities trading company.
quotes: In February 2026, the Company entered into a one-year time charter agreement with a global commodities trading company, for its VLCC vessel Nissos Nikouria, at a rate of $91,140 per day.

business_model.basis: stated in the risk factor summary; the commodity trader example is from Item 4
business_model.claim: Customers are charterers, including commodity trading companies. The company says it depends on a limited number of customers for a large part of its revenue.
quotes: Our dependence on a limited number of customers for a large part of our revenue

business_model.basis: stated in the Q3 results release; the segment interpretation is inferred
business_model.claim: The company reports separate daily time charter equivalent (TCE) rates for its VLCC and Suezmax fleets. VLCC earned much more per day than Suezmax in the latest reported quarter. No formal operating segments are shown in the evidence.
quotes: In Q3 2026, fleetwide daily TCE rate* of $206,800 per available spot day and $209,100 per operating day; VLCC TCE rate of $269,300 per available spot day and $260,100 per operating day; and Suezmax TCE rate of $166,600 per available spot and operating day.

business_model.claim: Revenue is driven by charter rates, the number of operating days and the mix of time-charter versus voyage-charter business. Spot employment makes revenue less predictable but can lift margins when tanker rates improve.
quotes: Revenues are affected by charter rates and the number of operating days.
Vessels operating in the spot charter market generate revenues that are less predictable, but can yield increased profit margins during periods of improvements in tankers rates.

business_model.claim: In the last full year, revenue was nearly flat because the daily TCE rate was almost unchanged, mainly reflecting spot employment of the fleet.
quotes: Revenue was $391.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, a decrease of $1.7 million, from $393.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2024.
Daily Time Charter Equivalent Rates decreased to $52,823 for the year ended December 31, 2025, from $52,898 for the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily due to the spot employment of the fleet.

business_model.basis: stated in the Q3 release; the rate-driven explanation is partly inferred from the TCE figures
business_model.claim: Revenue rose sharply in the latest reported quarter versus the year-earlier quarter. The release ties this to much higher daily TCE rates, with a series of VLCC short-term charters at very high daily rates.
quotes: Revenues of $501.5 million in Q3 2026, compared to $90.6 million in Q3 2025.
During Q3 2026, we entered into a series of short-term charter agreements for five of our VLCC vessels, for a period of 100-150 days each, with an average rate of $449,200 per day.

business_model.basis: stated in Item 5 (the $121.9 million total is printed in the voyage expenses discussion)
business_model.claim: Voyage expenses (fuel, port and canal costs) are the largest cost line under spot trading. They fell in the last full year on fewer miles sailed and lower fuel consumption.
quotes: Voyage expenses mainly relate to voyage charter agreements and consist of port, canal and bunker costs that are unique to a particular voyage and are recognized as incurred.
Fuel cost decreased from $88.7 million for the year ended December 31, 2024 to $81.4 million for the year ended December 31, 2025.

business_model.basis: stated in Item 5; the $45.2 million figure is printed in the opex discussion
business_model.claim: Vessel operating expenses cover crewing, insurance, repairs and stores and rose with inflation in the last full year. Management says insurance and crew cost pressures may continue.
quotes: Vessel operating expenses comprise all expenses relating to the operation of the vessel, including crewing, insurance, repairs and maintenance, stores, lubricants, spares and consumables and miscellaneous expenses.
The increase was mainly due to inflation.

business_model.claim: Technical management is outsourced to a related party, KMC, for a fixed daily fee per vessel, and commercial management sits with a wholly owned subsidiary. The fee per vessel per day was raised from $900 to $980 from the start of the current year.
quotes: We have entered into management agreements with OET Chartering Inc. (a wholly owned subsidiary) as commercial manager of our vessels and with KMC as our technical manager.
Effective January 1, 2026, the daily fee increased to $980 per vessel.

business_model.basis: stated in Item 5; the link to fleet growth is inferred
business_model.claim: Depreciation is a fixed-style cost. Vessels are depreciated straight-line over 25 years from delivery, after residual value, so it rises as vessels are added.
quotes: We depreciate all our vessels on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives, which we estimate to be 25 years from the date of their initial delivery from the shipyard, after considering their estimated residual value.

business_model.claim: Financing cost is a major expense because the business is debt funded. Interest expense and other finance costs fell as average debt and loan margins fell. Interest on SOFR-based loans can rise with rate hikes.
quotes: interest expense and other finance cost was $44.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared to $57.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2024

Interest on our SOFR-based loans (or loans based on another reference rate or its successor) can increase following any interest rate hikes undertaken by financial authorities (such as central banks) in response to, among other things, inflation.

business_model.basis: stated in the Item 3.D risk factors; the contrast with the latest quarter is from P7
business_model.claim: Tanker demand is seasonal: it is typically stronger in winter and weaker in summer. Quarterly results can therefore swing, and the filing says revenue was historically weaker in the quarters ending in June and September.
quotes: Tanker markets are typically stronger in the winter months due to increased oil consumption in the northern hemisphere, but weaker in the summer months due to lower oil consumption in the northern hemisphere and refinery maintenance.

The evidence does not settle how many vessels were owned and operating at each date.

The sailing fleet consists of ten modern scrubber-fitted Suezmax tankers and eight modern scrubber-fitted VLCC tankers.
